Western Boxy SUVs with Round Headlights Have a New Player to Worry About: The iCAUR V25
21 photos
Photo: iCAUR
There is something about square-bodied SUVs with round headlights that immediately makes my skin tingle, but in a good way. Just picture the Ford Bronco, or the G-Class, or the newer Land Rovers.
The design targets a particular segment of the population: people who can afford to go off-roading in a vehicle that looks different, is very capable, and, if possible, packs as many luxurious features as possible.
Until recently, carmakers executing such designs had nothing to fear from Chinese carmakers, as they didn’t really seem interested in going after buyers in this segment. Something changed recently, so the world now has to deal with such vehicles made by the likes of Jetour and iCAUR.
It’s the latter that’s of interest to us today, as it has announced the official public debut of the mid-size V25 SUV. Ok, the design has been in the news for a while now, but it is this week that the company presented it in front of a public audience during the iCAUR International User Summit that took place in Wuhu, China.
As a reminder, iCAUR (which is also known as iCAR, which in turn is short for iCar Ecological Technology) is an offshoot of Chery International, and it has already tested the waters of carmaking with products the likes of the 03, V23, and V27.
An electrified SUV by trade, the V25 is joining the party as the company’s first product to target international markets in an organized fashion. It has already been confirmed as a player on the Australian market, and it will probably expand elsewhere pretty fast.
I said earlier that the established boxy SUVs in the Western world have a new player to worry about, and I really mean that. Design-wise, at least, as the way the V25 has been made to look is at the same time familiar and fresh, old-school and original, retro and futuristic.
As far as performance levels go, things look pretty decent as well, at least on paper. The SUV relies on a range extender system that blends together a 1.5-litre turbocharged 4-cylinder internal combustion engine rated at 154 hp that feeds electricity into a lithium-ion battery pack good for 93 miles (150 km, as measured under WLTC) on a single fill.
The company is probably using the land Down Under as a sort of test market for the future, and for now it did not confirm the arrival of the mid-size SUV on the European market. The UK will see the first iCAUR product in the form of the larger, flagship V27, which is scheduled to enter the local market early next year.
We’ll keep an eye on that, and also on the other exploits of this new car company, and report back once we know more.
